title: GCP VPCs: Global Networks and Regional Subnets
intro: GCP networking differs from AWS and Azure in one big way: a VPC network is global, and subnets are regional. One VPC can span every region with no peering. There are no route tables per subnet, and no NAT or internet gateways as separate objects you attach.

steps.prompt: List the VPC networks in the project.
steps.fake_output:
NAME      SUBNET_MODE  BGP_ROUTING_MODE  IPV4_RANGE  GATEWAY_IPV4
default   AUTO         REGIONAL
prod-vpc  CUSTOM       GLOBAL
steps.explanation: The auto-mode 'default' network, and a custom-mode prod-vpc.
steps.why: Auto mode creates a subnet in every region, with fixed ranges that overlap across projects, which makes peering impossible later. Production uses custom mode, where you choose the ranges. Many organisations block the default network with an org policy.

expected_commands: gcloud compute networks subnets list --network prod-vpc
steps.fake_output:
NAME          REGION        NETWORK   RANGE          STACK_TYPE
public-ew1    europe-west1  prod-vpc  10.10.0.0/20   IPV4_ONLY
private-ew1   europe-west1  prod-vpc  10.20.0.0/20   IPV4_ONLY
private-use1  us-east1      prod-vpc  10.30.0.0/20   IPV4_ONLY
steps.explanation: Subnets in two regions of the same network. VMs in both can talk over internal IPs directly.
steps.why: 'public' and 'private' are just names here: in GCP a VM is internet-facing only if it has an external IP (and the firewall allows it). Subnet design is about IP ranges and regions, not routing.

steps.prompt: Create a subnet private-ew4 in europe-west4 on prod-vpc with range 10.40.0.0/20, with Private Google Access enabled.
expected_commands: gcloud compute networks subnets create private-ew4 --network prod-vpc --region europe-west4 --range 10.40.0.0/20 --enable-private-ip-google-access
gcloud compute networks subnets create private-ew4 --network=prod-vpc --region=europe-west4 --range=10.40.0.0/20 --enable-private-ip-google-access
steps.fake_output:
Created [https://www.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/shop-prod-217733/regions/europe-west4/subnetworks/private-ew4].
NAME         REGION        NETWORK   RANGE          STACK_TYPE
private-ew4  europe-west4  prod-vpc  10.40.0.0/20   IPV4_ONLY
steps.explanation: A new regional subnet. VMs without external IPs in it can still reach Google APIs (Cloud Storage, BigQuery...).
steps.why: Private Google Access is GCP's equivalent of AWS gateway endpoints: private VMs reach Google services without NAT or public IPs. Without it, a private VM can't even pull from Artifact Registry. Turn it on for every private subnet.

steps.fake_output:
NAME                          NETWORK   DEST_RANGE    NEXT_HOP                  PRIORITY
default-route-4f2c8e1a7b3d    prod-vpc  0.0.0.0/0     default-internet-gateway  1000
default-route-r-10.10.0.0-20  prod-vpc  10.10.0.0/20  prod-vpc                  0
default-route-r-10.20.0.0-20  prod-vpc  10.20.0.0/20  prod-vpc                  0
steps.explanation: Subnet routes plus one default route to the internet gateway for the whole network.
steps.why: Routes belong to the network, not to subnets. The default internet route only works for VMs with an external IP. Private VMs need Cloud NAT (gcp-tutorial-006), and deleting the default route cuts off both, including Private Google Access.
